explanation: Passing under a torii marks the step from the everyday world into sacred ground. At Itsukushima Shrine, a huge torii stands in the sea and seems to float at high tide.

claims.text: Torii gates traditionally mark the entrance to Shinto shrines.
Torii are not the traditional entrance gates of Buddhist, Taoist or Confucian temples.
A torii marks the transition from the ordinary world to sacred space.
The torii of Itsukushima Shrine stands in the sea and appears to float at high tide.
